First, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-6{x}^{7}) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-6\cdot {x}^{7}) \\  & =-6\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{7}$ is a power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{7}=-\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the negative constant $-6$ changes the sign of the limit. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-6\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{7} & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{7}=\infty . & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-6{x}^{7})=\infty .
$$
